title: EAS-Sim: A Framework and its Methodology for the Co-Design of Multi-Objective, Energy-Aware Schedulers for AI Clusters
problem: Energy consumption is a critical operational cost in DL cluster datacenters, but schedulers ignore energy objectives
motivation: Modern HPC datacenters need multi-objective schedulers balancing performance, fairness, QoS, and energy efficiency
method: EAS-Sim is a simulation-based tool for designing job schedulers that handle multiple competing objectives in AI clusters. The methodology guides the design of different scheduler variants: Zeus for minimizing energy, Hades for ensuring fairness, AuraChronos for meeting service-level agreements, and Charon for respecting power budget limits.
key_novelty: The framework enables systematic design of job schedulers that optimize energy efficiency alongside fairness, service-level agreements, and power constraints.
